Multi-Seasonal Portmanteau Tests

Source: R/portmanteau.R
msportmanteau.Rd

Multi-seasonal generalisation of the Ljung-Box and Monti portmanteau tests: residual autocorrelation is checked at low-order and seasonal lags at once, for an arbitrary number of seasonal periods.

Usage

msportmanteau(
  x,
  type = c("Ljung-Box", "Monti"),
  season = NULL,
  nlag = 5,
  lags_short = 0,
  npar = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A numeric vector, a ts/msts object, or a fitted msarima model (in which case the model residuals are used).

type

Either "Ljung-Box" (default), which builds the statistic from the autocorrelations, or "Monti", which uses the partial autocorrelations. Partial matching is allowed.

season

Numeric vector of seasonal periods to test, of any length. If NULL (default) the periods are taken from the msts/ts attributes of x, or from the fitted model.

nlag

Numeric vector giving the number of seasonal multiples of each period to test, i.e. lags season * (1:nlag). A single value is recycled across season; otherwise give one value per period, e.g. c(5, 3). Default 5.

lags_short

Number of low-order, non-seasonal lags 1:lags_short added to the seasonal ones. Default 0 (none).

npar

Number of estimated model parameters. Default 0 for a raw series; for a fitted msarima model it defaults to the number of estimated (non-fixed) AR, seasonal AR, MA and seasonal MA coefficients.

Value

An object of class "htest", with:

statistic

the test statistic ("X-squared").

parameter

the degrees of freedom ("df"), the number of lags tested minus npar.

p.value

the p-value, from the upper tail of a chi-squared distribution with parameter degrees of freedom.

method

a character string describing the test.

data.name

a character string naming the data.

lag

the lags actually tested.

Details

The lag set tested is sort(unique(c(1:lags_short, outer(season, 1:nlag)))), the same construction as in the original two-season versions of these tests, generalised to any number of periods.

As in sacf, leading and trailing NAs (such as those produced by differencing in msarima) are dropped (stats::na.contiguous) before computing the statistic, and the number of observations used is the length of the series that remains.

References

Grigoletto, M. and Lisi, F. (2026). Portmanteau goodness-of-fit tests in the presence of simple, mixed, and multiple seasonal autocorrelation. arXiv. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2609.32381

Ljung, G. M. and Box, G. E. P. (1978). On a measure of lack of fit in time series models. Biometrika, 65(2), 297-303.

Monti, A. C. (1994). A proposal for a residual autocorrelation test in linear models. Biometrika, 81(4), 776-780.

See also

sacf, msarima, stats::Box.test

Examples

fit <- msarima(MAD_m40, order = c(1, 0, 2),
               seasonal = list(c(0, 1, 1), c(0, 1, 1)))

# periods 24 and 168 taken from the msts object
msportmanteau(MAD_m40, nlag = 3)
#> 
#> 	Multi-seasonal Ljung-Box test
#> 
#> data:  MAD_m40
#> X-squared = 4767.5, df = 6, p-value < 2.2e-16
#> 
# residual test, periods and npar from the model
msportmanteau(fit, type = "Monti", nlag = 3)
#> 
#> 	Multi-seasonal Monti test
#> 
#> data:  MAD_m40
#> X-squared = 3.8858, df = 1, p-value = 0.0487
#>
